- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.5) — model fails to capture bearish momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — model overcorrects, leading to overprediction in subsequent days.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model often forecasts prices to revert to historical mean, but fails to account for sustained momentum.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment changes, especially when sentiment drops sharply.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overpredict early days (1–5) when sentiment is rising, then underpredict later days (15–30) when sentiment is falling or neutral.
- Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is declining and price is rising — model ignores sentiment-driven reversal signals.
- Avoid overfitting to recent price trends — model often follows recent highs without considering sentiment-driven corrections.
